name: Photorealism
summary: Paintings that copy a photograph in every detail: glass, chrome, signs and street reflections, in sharp, even focus. The hand is hidden and the picture is as cool as a camera.

philosophy.core_thesis: A painting can match the camera: the artist works from a photograph, keeps its sharp focus and its flat modern light, and shows the city as the lens sees it.
design_principles: Work from a photograph, and transfer it by a grid or a projector, with an error of under 2%.
Keep the whole picture in sharp focus, with detail down to 1–2mm in the background.
Choose urban, banal subjects: a shop front, a car, a diner, a street, a sign, a window.
Paint reflections in glass and chrome, with 2–4 reflected scenes layered over the main view.
Hold an even, flat light with no drama, in a clear, high-key daylight.
Hide the brush: smooth, blended paint, with an airbrush or a fine brush for the gradients.
Show no comment on the subject, and keep the mood neutral and cool.
anti_patterns: A soft, blurred or selective focus
A dramatic, moody or romantic light
A heroic, historical or allegorical subject
A flattened, abstracted or simplified form
A painted comment on the subject, such as satire

composition.layout: A frontal or three-quarter street view with a flat, even light, strong perspective lines to a vanishing point, and layers of reflection in glass.
composition.focal_point: A shop window, a car or a sign, at one third from an edge; there is no single dramatic centre, and the detail is equal across the picture.
composition.format: A large canvas at 3:2 to 2:1, 1.5m or more wide, so that the detail reads as a photograph.

principles.rule: Run the kerb, the roof line and the shop front to one vanishing point, with all lines within 2° of the true perspective.
Build 3–4 layers: the reflected street, the glass, the shop interior and the far background, each in sharp focus.
Repeat a window, a sign or a car 4–12 times in perspective, with the step shrinking at the correct rate.
Hold one flat daylight and one level of focus across the picture, with detail at 1–2mm everywhere.
Frame the view by the edge of a building or a window, and cut the scene as a camera crop does.
Group the signs, the cars and the lights in clusters of 3–5 items, as they sit in the photograph.

palette.strategy: The colour of a colour photograph of the period: bright signs and chrome set in a mid-tone street, with blue-grey reflections and a pale sky.
palette.distribution: Street and building mid-tones 40–50%, sky and glass reflections 25–30%, bright signs and cars 15–20%, dark shadows 5–10%.
palette.ground: A white, smooth acrylic ground, sanded between coats.

brushwork_and_medium.medium: Acrylic or thin oil, applied with an airbrush, a fine brush and a razor for highlights.
brushwork_and_medium.support: Primed canvas, smooth, 1.5m or more wide.
brushwork_and_medium.brushwork: None in view: smooth, thin, blended layers; fine sable strokes of 1–2mm for sign and chrome detail.
brushwork_and_medium.paint_handling: 8–20 thin layers; the surface is smooth and the paint shows no ridge.
brushwork_and_medium.edges: Sharp where the photograph is sharp, with exact highlights of 1–3mm on glass and chrome.

light_and_modelling.light: Flat, bright, even daylight, as the camera caught it; no drama and no clear time of day.
light_and_modelling.modelling: Smooth and exact, in 8–10 steps; the gradients on chrome and glass are airbrushed.
light_and_modelling.shadow: Short, mid-value and neutral; 15–25% of the area, with a sharp edge.
light_and_modelling.temperature: Neutral to slightly cool; warm signs and cars against cool glass and sky.

subject.typical: A shop front, a car park, a diner, a street with signs, a window with reflections, a suburban house with a car.
subject.figure_scale: People are few and small, at 5–10% of the picture height, or absent.
subject.treatment: Cool and deadpan; the view is plain, urban and exact, and offers no comment.

surface.finish: Satin to gloss and smooth, like a print.
surface.texture: Flat; no ridge and no stroke in view.

reference_works.note: Object ids were checked against the Art Institute of Chicago API. None of the three works is flagged as public domain by the museum: the ids identify them only. Look at the museum page for the image and its licence; do not copy it.

emotion.target_response: Cool wonder: the viewer admires the exact copy, and feels the flat, bright look of the modern street.

use_cases: automotive, retail and city campaign art
product scenes with exact glass and metal
book covers with a flat, modern look
avoid_when: The brief needs expression, a hand-made touch or a loose mood.
The picture must be abstract, symbolic or romantic.

modifiers.how: Flatten the detail to hard shapes, raise the chroma, add a halftone dot of 1–3mm, and choose a single brand or a product as the subject.
Drop the photograph and the airbrush; use a brown, earthy key, a visible stroke of 5–15mm, and ordinary people at work in side light.

brush_size.note: The paint is blended and airbrushed, so no stroke shows.

sources.title: Art Institute of Chicago API (CC0 data)
Louis K. Meisel, Photorealism (Harry N. Abrams, 1980)
